theme: Fructose, pentose-phosphate and gluconeogenic sugar-phosphate interconversion
story: The centre is the hub of hexose-phosphate traffic: fructose metabolism (fructose 6-phosphate, fructose 1,6-bisphosphate, fructose catabolism and biosynthesis) linked to gluconeogenesis from pyruvate, lactate, alanine, oxaloacetate and glycerol-3-phosphate. Around it sit the non-oxidative pentose-phosphate shunt (RPIA and TALDO1 deficiencies, xylulose-5-phosphate formation) and the glucuronate-xylulose route with its pentosuria, plus galactose and fructose inborn errors (GALK1, GALE, essential fructosuria, hereditary fructose intolerance). Together they describe how dietary sugars, polyols and three-carbon precursors are funnelled into and out of the shared glycolytic/gluconeogenic intermediates, with phosphocreatine and resveratrol response as peripheral additions.

theme: Peroxisomal fatty acid alpha- and beta-oxidation
story: The core is peroxisomal lipid breakdown: acyl-CoA oxidase-driven beta-oxidation of very-long-chain fatty acids and pristanoyl-CoA, preceded by alpha-oxidation of branched phytanate. Medium- and long-chain acyl-CoA catabolism, malonyl-CoA and succinyl-CoA handling represent the shared acyl-CoA bookkeeping that links peroxisomal shortening to further oxidation, and TYSND1 processing of peroxisomal enzymes supports the machinery. The cluster as a whole is about degrading fatty acids that mitochondria cannot handle directly.

theme: Xenobiotic and drug metabolism (phase I/II biotransformation)
story: The centre is xenobiotic biotransformation: cytochrome P450 (CYP1A2, CYP2E1) and FMO oxidations, followed by phase II conjugations such as sulfonation, methylation (TPMT), acetylation and glycine/glutamine conjugation of aromatic acids. Drug ADME pathways (paracetamol, aspirin, azathioprine, prednisone, atorvastatin, ciprofloxacin), aflatoxin activation, ethanol oxidation and AhR signalling are instances or inducers of this machinery, while plant compound classes (flavones, monoterpenoids, phenylpropanoids, alkaloids, polyketides) are its substrates. The cluster as a whole is the liver-centred system for chemically modifying and detoxifying foreign compounds and drugs.

theme: Cytosolic RNA sensing driving type I interferon antiviral response
story: The core is RIG-I/MDA5 (DDX58/IFIH1) and DEx/H-box helicase sensing of viral dsRNA, signalling through TRAF3 and IRF3 to induce interferon-alpha/beta, with positive and negative regulators of RIG-I signalling. Parallel TLR7/8/9 routes via TRAF6-IRF7 and NF-kB activation (FADD/RIP1, ZBP1) feed the same interferon and inflammatory output, and downstream effectors such as OAS and the antiviral IFN signature execute it. Viral evasion (RSV) and activated dendritic cells frame this as the innate antiviral defence system.

theme: Monoamine neurotransmitter reuptake and vesicular loading
story: The centre is clearance of catecholamines from the synapse by SLC6 transporters: norepinephrine uptake via SLC6A2 and dopamine reuptake via SLC6A3. Disease entries show the consequences of their failure (orthostatic intolerance, infantile parkinsonism-dystonia), and vesicular loading completes the recycling loop. The cluster describes how monoamine signalling is terminated and transmitter is recycled.

theme: Scavenger receptor clearance of apoptotic cells and modified lipoproteins
story: The centre is phagocytic clearance: recognition of phosphatidylserine-exposing apoptotic cells, engulfment and efferocytosis, including neutrophil and immune complex clearance. Scavenger receptors of classes A, B, F and H provide the uptake machinery, and because they also bind modified lipoproteins they link to cholesterol storage and macrophage foam cell formation. The cluster as a whole is about macrophages removing dying cells and debris, with atherogenic lipid uptake as a side consequence.

theme: Initiation and control of mitotic DNA replication
story: The core is S-phase DNA replication: initiation at origins, DNA unwinding and the regulation of replication firing. E2F-driven G1/S transcription and cell cycle modules supply the gene programme that licenses entry, while ATR activation and the replication checkpoint restrain replication under stress. Together the pathways describe how proliferating cells start and safeguard genome duplication.

theme: Urea cycle and ammonia detoxification
story: The centre is the hepatic urea cycle: CPS1, OTC, ASS1, ASL and ARG1 converting ammonia via citrulline, argininosuccinate and arginine to urea, with NAGS activation and the SLC25A15 ornithine carrier. The many disease pathways are the inborn errors of each step, and aspartate, ornithine and arginine metabolism supply the cycle's intermediates. Ammonium homeostasis and transcriptional control frame the cluster as the body's system for disposing of nitrogen.

theme: M-CSF signalling in macrophage and osteoclast development
story: The centre is CSF1 (M-CSF) receptor signalling, which drives macrophage proliferation and fusion and osteoclast differentiation. Osteoclast fusion, proliferation and positive/negative regulation of bone resorption and remodelling are the bone-facing outcome of this pathway. Interleukin SHC signalling and IL-37 are adjacent cytokine-receptor modules; overall the cluster describes how myeloid growth-factor signalling generates bone-resorbing cells.

theme: Type 2 immunity: Th2, IL-33 and eosinophils
story: The core is Th2 differentiation and production of IL-4, IL-5 and IL-13, triggered in part by the alarmin IL-33. Eosinophil chemotaxis, migration, activation and effector immunity, together with mast cell activation, are the downstream effector arm. The cluster as a whole is the type 2 response used against helminths (response to nematode) and responsible for allergic inflammation.

theme: Fructose metabolism and gluconeogenesis via glycerol
story: The centre is fructose handling: fructose catabolism, fructose 6-phosphate and 1,6-bisphosphate interconversion, and its inborn errors (essential fructosuria, hereditary fructose intolerance). Gluconeogenesis and fructose biosynthesis run the same steps in reverse, with glycerol, glycerol-3-phosphate and other alditols and alanine as gluconeogenic feeders. Overall the cluster describes the hepatic interconversion of fructose, triose and glycerol carbon with glucose production; resveratrol response is peripheral.

theme: Canonical and non-canonical NF-kB pathway regulation
story: The core is NF-kB activation: IKK complex recruitment via RIP1, IRAK1 and linear ubiquitination downstream of TNFR1, TLRs and CD40, plus NIK-driven non-canonical signalling from TNF superfamily receptors and Dectin-1. Deubiquitination, SUMOylation and negative regulators shape signal strength, while IKBKG, IKBKB and IkBA defects (EDA-ID, SCID) show the consequences of breaking it. Adjacent TNFR1 proapoptotic signalling and TPL2-MAPK activation share the same receptor complexes; overall the cluster is about how inflammatory receptors switch NF-kB transcription on and off.

theme: Complement cascade activation and regulation
story: The centre is the complement cascade: classical antibody-mediated and alternative pathway activation converging on C3 and C5 cleavage. Positive and negative regulators of each pathway and of opsonization keep the cascade targeted and prevent host damage. The cluster as a whole is the humoral innate system that tags, lyses and inflames against pathogens and immune complexes.

theme: Neutral and imino amino acid transport and its disorders
story: The core is plasma-membrane transport of neutral amino acids, proline and glycine by SLC6A19, SLC6A20 and proton-coupled SLC36A2. Hartnup disorder and iminoglycinuria/hyperglycinuria represent failure of these renal and intestinal absorptive transporters, and tryptophan transport is one of their key substrates. Overall the cluster describes epithelial amino acid reabsorption.

theme: GPCR-mediated chemotaxis of neutrophils and monocytes
story: The centre is leukocyte chemotaxis driven by chemoattractant G protein-coupled receptors, notably formyl peptide receptors sensing bacterial and danger peptides. Production of chemokines such as MCP-1 and MIP-1 alpha and regulation of neutrophil, granulocyte and macrophage chemotaxis describe the recruitment output. Activated monocyte/dendritic cell signatures and cellular defence frame this as innate cell recruitment to sites of infection.

theme: Kidney development: ureteric bud and nephron formation
story: The centre is metanephric kidney organogenesis: reciprocal induction between the ureteric bud (branching, elongation, collecting duct) and metanephric mesenchyme (renal vesicle, comma- and S-shaped bodies, nephron tubules, loop of Henle). Earlier stages (intermediate mesoderm, pronephros, mesonephros, nephric duct) and patterning and size control give the developmental sequence. The cluster as a whole describes how the urinary system is built.

theme: Glutamate and GABA reuptake at synapses
story: The core is clearance of amino acid neurotransmitters: glutamate reuptake by excitatory amino acid transporters (SLC1A3, with D-aspartate as substrate) and GABA reuptake. The astrocytic glutamate-glutamine cycle and GABA metabolism recycle the transmitter, and vesicular loading (SLC17A8) refills synaptic vesicles. Disease entries (episodic ataxia, DFNA25 deafness) show the cost of failures in this excitatory/inhibitory transmitter recycling system.

theme: GPCR signalling in platelet activation
story: The centre is platelet activation via G protein-coupled receptors: ADP through P2Y1 and P2Y12, thrombin through PARs, and thromboxane through TP. GPVI collagen signalling and LDL sensitisation add further activating inputs, while prostacyclin signalling provides the inhibitory counterbalance. Together they describe how soluble agonists amplify platelet activation during haemostasis.

theme: ESCRT-mediated multivesicular body sorting and membrane scission
story: The core is the ESCRT machinery: sorting ubiquitinated cargo into multivesicular bodies, membrane fission and ESCRT disassembly. Its applications are EGFR downregulation and ubiquitin-dependent receptor endocytosis, exosome assembly and secretion, and non-lytic viral release, with Listeria InlB entry exploiting the same endocytic route. Overall the cluster is about how cells internalise, degrade or release membrane cargo through endosomal budding.

theme: Erythrocyte gas exchange and ammonium transport
story: The centre is red cell gas exchange: uptake of oxygen and release of carbon dioxide in lungs and the reverse in tissues, with intracellular oxygen and nitric oxide transport. Rhesus glycoproteins (RHAG and relatives) form the gas/ammonium channel arm, carrying CO2 and ammonium across red cells and epithelia; RHAG defects cause Rh-null haemolytic anaemia. The cluster as a whole describes membrane transport of small gaseous and nitrogenous solutes.

theme: Coronavirus genome replication and host translation hijacking
story: The core is the SARS-CoV-1/2 replication cycle: translation of replicase polyproteins with frameshifting, their maturation, assembly of the replication-transcription complex, genome replication and viral mRNA synthesis and capping. The other members describe how the virus subverts host translation, mRNA processing and RNA silencing and evades IFIT and PKR, and how the host perturbs viral replication. Overall the cluster is about positive-strand RNA virus replication and its contest with host gene-expression machinery.

theme: RNA polymerase I transcription of ribosomal RNA
story: The centre is rDNA transcription by RNA polymerase I: preinitiation complex assembly, promoter opening and escape, elongation and termination. Nucleolar chromatin regulators (NoRC and SIRT1 repressing, B-WICH and CSB/G9a activating) set how many rDNA repeats are active, and Pol III 5S rRNA transcription supplies the remaining rRNA. The cluster describes how cells produce ribosomal RNA for ribosome biogenesis.

theme: ER tubular network shaping and non-vesicular lipid transfer
story: The centre is the endoplasmic reticulum's tubular network: membrane bending, tubule formation, ER fusion and ER-plasma membrane tethering. These contact sites host intermembrane lipid transfer, moving PI, PC and cholesterol between the ER, Golgi and other membranes, with PI synthesis supplying the lipid. Overall the cluster is about ER membrane architecture and the lipid exchange it supports.

theme: Renin-angiotensin regulation of blood pressure and volume
story: The core is the renin-angiotensin system: processing of angiotensinogen to angiotensins, angiotensin receptor signalling and control of angiotensin levels. Its outputs are renal sodium excretion, urine volume, blood volume and systemic arterial pressure. Bradykinin and neuropeptide catabolism reflect the shared peptidases (ACE and related enzymes) that degrade vasoactive peptides.

theme: E2F-driven G1/S transition and replication origin licensing
story: The centre is E2F transcription at G1/S, which induces the genes needed for S phase (E2F targets, G1/S-specific transcription). Origin licensing steps (ORC, CDC6 association, pre-replicative complex activation, Orc1 removal) are the direct mechanistic link to DNA replication initiation. Replication checkpoint and ATR activation guard the process; overall the cluster describes the commitment to and start of DNA replication.

theme: Receptor tyrosine kinase signalling to PI3K/AKT and ERK
story: The core is RTK autophosphorylation (IGF1R, ALK, LTK) recruiting adaptors such as IRS and SHC. These branch into PI3K/AKT activation (including AKT2 and glycogen synthesis) and SOS-Ras-ERK1/2 signalling, with PP2A/IER3 regulation, signal attenuation and constitutive PI3K activation in cancer. The cluster describes the shared growth-factor signalling backbone downstream of tyrosine kinase receptors.

theme: Membrane transport of xenobiotics and drugs
story: The centre is transporter-mediated movement of foreign compounds: uptake by SLCO organic anion and SLC organic cation transporters and efflux across cell membranes and the blood-brain barrier. Drug ADME entries (atorvastatin, ciprofloxacin, abacavir) and glycoside and flavone handling are examples of substrates. Overall the cluster is about the transport phase of drug disposition.

theme: Gonadotropin control of ovarian follicle maturation and ovulation
story: The centre is ovarian follicle development: antral follicle growth, oocyte meiotic maturation, ovulation and luteinization. LH and FSH secretion, with its positive and negative regulation, provides the pituitary drive, and Sertoli cell proliferation and gonad development reflect the parallel testicular and developmental side. Together the cluster describes the hormonal programme leading to ovulation.

theme: Actin filament assembly and turnover in protrusion and macropinocytosis
story: The core is actin dynamics: Arp2/3 nucleation, barbed-end capping, severing, depolymerisation and crosslinking into networks. These drive membrane protrusions such as ruffles and podosomes, actin-based motility and macropinocytosis/pinocytosis. Caspase cleavage of cytoskeletal proteins shows dismantling of the same network; overall the cluster is about how the actin cytoskeleton remodels membranes.

theme: Tryptophan-kynurenine route to NAD+ and redox detoxification
story: The centre is tryptophan catabolism through kynurenine and quinolinate to de novo NAD+ synthesis, together with nicotinate metabolism, pyridine nucleotide salvage and NAD+ breakdown. A second arm covers handling of reactive carbonyls: methylglyoxal and aldehyde detoxification and repair of damaged proteins, linked to cellular redox state. Overall the cluster is about maintaining NAD+ supply and protecting cells from metabolic by-products.

theme: Insulin secretion and insulin action in glucose homeostasis
story: The centre is the beta cell: glucose-stimulated insulin secretion and its modulation by incretins (GLP-1, GIP), free fatty acid receptors (GPR40), acetylcholine, KATP (ABCC8) and K+ channels, plus insulin processing. The other arm is insulin action: receptor signalling via IRS and AKT2, GLUT4 translocation, glucose import and glycogen synthesis, with receptor recycling, attenuation, insulin degradation and adiponectin. Together they describe the endocrine loop that controls blood glucose.

theme: Amino acid and choline neurotransmitter synthesis, uptake and recycling
story: The core is glutamate and GABA handling: excitatory amino acid transporter reuptake (SLC1A1, SLC1A3), astrocytic glutamate-glutamine cycling, and GABA synthesis, secretion, reuptake and degradation. Glycine transport (SLC6A5, hyperekplexia) and choline uptake for acetylcholine synthesis (SLC5A7, motor neuronopathy) extend this to other small transmitters, and disease entries mark each transporter's failure. Bile acid and alkanesulfonate transport are peripheral SLC members; overall the cluster is about supplying and clearing small-molecule neurotransmitters.

theme: Mitotic centrosome maturation and spindle positioning
story: The centre is mitotic centrosome maturation: recruitment of centrosome proteins, loss of Nlp and AURKA activation by TPX2 to promote spindle assembly. NuMA recruitment and astral microtubule organisation then position and orient the spindle. The cluster as a whole describes how dividing cells build and place the mitotic spindle.

theme: B cell activation, germinal centre and plasma cell differentiation
story: The core is B cell development and activation captured by B cell, memory B cell and plasma cell/immunoglobulin signatures. Tfh differentiation and ICOS co-stimulation provide T cell help, enabling germinal centre B cell and plasma cell differentiation and adaptive memory. Overall the cluster describes the T-dependent humoral response that generates antibody-secreting and memory B cells.

theme: Androgen and other steroid hormone receptor signalling
story: The centre is androgen receptor signalling: AR-driven transcription of KLK2/KLK3, the androgen response programme, testosterone response and synthesis, and negative regulation of AR, including in prostate epithelium. Estrogen and progesterone responses and the HSP90 chaperone cycle for ligand-bound steroid receptors represent the shared nuclear receptor machinery. The cluster as a whole is about steroid hormones controlling gene expression in reproductive tissues.

theme: Chromatin remodelling during DNA repair and replication
story: The centre is nucleosome organisation: disassembly and reassembly of protein-DNA complexes, replication-dependent chromatin assembly and CHD1/CHD2 remodellers. DNA repair-dependent remodelling, nucleotide-excision repair regulation and ADP-ribosylation control link this to damage repair. Overall the cluster describes how chromatin is opened and restored so DNA can be repaired or copied.

theme: DNA double-strand break response and repair
story: The core is DSB repair: sensing breaks, ATM signalling, and repair by homologous recombination (strand invasion, SDSA, break-induced replication, resolution), classical and alternative NHEJ, and MMEJ, with BRCA1/BARD1/BRCA2 defects. Interstrand cross-link repair (Fanconi anaemia), replication fork reversal, R-loop processing and responses to genotoxic drugs (cisplatin, camptothecin, bleomycin, hydroxyurea) represent replication-associated damage, while PARylation, ubiquitination, checkpoints and DNA topology changes regulate the response. The cluster as a whole is the genome-maintenance system for broken and stalled DNA.

theme: Axon guidance by netrin and semaphorin cues
story: The centre is axon guidance: growth cones extending and turning in response to netrin (attraction and repulsion) and semaphorin-plexin signals. Specific instances such as serotonergic and sympathetic axon guidance, anterior/posterior guidance and target innervation show the outcome. Overall the cluster describes how neurons wire to their targets.

theme: Nutrient and energy sensing by mTORC1
story: The centre is mTORC1 signalling and its positive and negative control. Amino acid sensing (leucine, methionine), energy sensing via LKB1-AMPK, glucose starvation and AKT inhibition of the TSC complex are the inputs that converge on Rheb-mTORC1. The cluster as a whole describes how cells match growth and translation to nutrient availability.

theme: Platelet adhesion, activation and degranulation in haemostasis
story: The centre is platelet adhesion to exposed collagen via VWF-GPIb-IX-V and GPVI, followed by activation, aggregation and degranulation (SNARE-mediated). VWF and GP1BA variant and ADAMTS13 cleavage disorders show how altered adhesion causes bleeding or thrombosis, while PECAM1 and negative regulators restrain aggregation. Overall the cluster describes the primary haemostatic plug and its link to blood coagulation.

theme: IFN-gamma, Th1 and dendritic cell antigen presentation
story: The core is the type 1 axis: dendritic cell IL-12 production driving Th1 differentiation and IFN-gamma production, with the IFN-gamma response programme. IFN-gamma in turn upregulates MHC class I and II for antigen presentation to CD4 and CD8 T cells, and TLR/MyD88 signalling and GM-CSF supply the innate activating input. The cluster as a whole describes cell-mediated immunity against intracellular pathogens.

theme: Base excision repair of damaged DNA bases
story: The centre is base excision repair: DNA glycosylases (OGG1, NTHL1, MUTYH, NEIL1/3) recognise and cleave damaged purines and pyrimidines, APEX1 processes the abasic site, and POLB short-patch or PCNA-dependent long-patch synthesis fills the gap. The many defective-glycosylase entries document disease-linked failures of the recognition step, and single-strand break repair and NEIL3 interstrand cross-link resolution are close relatives. Overall the cluster is the pathway that removes oxidised and modified bases from DNA.

theme: tRNA and rRNA processing, modification and aminoacylation
story: The core is tRNA maturation: 5' leader and 3' end processing, intron splicing, and many modifications (methylation, pseudouridylation, wybutosine, wobble and t6A modifications) in nucleus and mitochondrion, followed by cytosolic and mitochondrial aminoacylation. rRNA methylation and pseudouridylation and mRNA modification/editing extend the same RNA-modifying enzymology. The cluster as a whole is about producing correctly modified RNAs that ensure translational fidelity.

theme: RUNX2-driven osteoblast differentiation and bone formation
story: The centre is RUNX2, the master transcription factor regulated to drive osteoblast differentiation and development. Its outcomes are bone formation by direct (intramembranous) ossification, trabecular bone and cranial sutures. Cartilage and tendon development are neighbouring skeletal tissues; overall the cluster describes building the skeleton.

theme: Cation-chloride cotransport, renal salt handling and cell volume
story: The centre is the SLC12 cation-chloride cotransporters (NKCC2, NCC, KCC3) and chloride exchangers that move Na+, K+ and Cl- across epithelia, with Bartter, Gitelman and chloride diarrhoea showing renal and intestinal consequences. Osmosensory signalling and hyper/hypotonic responses reflect the same transporters' role in cell volume regulation, alongside potassium channels and paracellular transport. Overall the cluster is about salt transport for renal balance and cell volume homeostasis.

theme: TGF-beta, activin and BMP signalling and its regulation
story: The core is TGF-beta superfamily signalling through receptors to SMAD2/3:SMAD4 transcription, including BMP, activin and NODAL branches. Extracellular regulation (follistatin, TGFBR3 co-receptor, ligand sequestration in matrix) and intracellular downregulation tune the signal, and cancer mutations in TGFBR1/2 and SMADs show its disruption. The cluster as a whole describes how this ligand family is delivered, gated and transduced.

theme: Hexosamine, sialic acid and nucleotide-sugar supply for glycosylation
story: The centre is nucleotide-sugar production: the hexosamine pathway from fructose 6-phosphate (GFPT1) to UDP-GlcNAc, UDP-glucose and UDP-glucuronate, and sialic acid synthesis to CMP-sialic acid (GNE). SLC35 transporters move these donors into the Golgi and ER, and the many CDG and myasthenic disease entries mark failures of supply or transport. Overall the cluster is about providing the sugar donors for protein and lipid glycosylation.

theme: Cholesterol efflux and reverse cholesterol transport
story: The centre is cellular cholesterol efflux to apolipoprotein A-I/HDL, controlled by LXR (NR1H3/NR1H2) target genes. Regulation of HDL clearance, reverse cholesterol transport and sterol homeostasis define the systemic arm, while limits on cholesterol storage, foam cell formation and pinocytosis are the macrophage outcome. The cluster as a whole is about removing excess cholesterol from peripheral cells, protecting against atherosclerosis.

theme: Gonad development, germ cells and gonadotropin control of reproduction
story: The core is gonadotropin signalling: GnRH, LH and FSH secretion and cellular responses that drive Leydig, Sertoli and follicle function. Germ cell biology (primordial germ cell migration, proliferation, meiosis entry, programmed death) and testis/ovary development supply the gametes, while ovulation, luteinization, luteolysis and the oestrous cycle are the female cyclic outcomes. Overall the cluster describes the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis and the development it controls.

theme: Post-transcriptional mRNA control by RBPs and small RNAs
story: The centre is regulation of mRNA fate after transcription: AU-rich element binding proteins (TTP, AUF1, KSRP, BRF1 destabilising; HuR, IGF2BPs stabilising) controlling deadenylation, decapping and 5'-3' decay. The microRNA/siRNA arm (biogenesis, RISC assembly, target-directed miRNA decay, silencing by translational repression or destabilisation of specific mRNAs) is the second regulatory layer. Together they describe how cells set mRNA stability and translation.
